subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If the coefficients of 4 consecutive terms in the expansion of (1 + x)ⁿ are a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄ respectively, then show that a₁/(a₁ + a₂) + a₃/(a₃ + a₄) = 2a₂/(a₂ + a₃).

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — what the four coefficients are, the one identity that turns each fraction into (r + 1)/(n + 1), what the left side and the right side each reduce to, and why they are equal.
insider_note: The four coefficients start at a general r — ⁿCᵣ to ⁿCᵣ₊₃, never ⁿC₁ to ⁿC₄. The seventh mark is the one-line sentence that the reduced left and right sides are the same expression; reducing both and never saying so loses it.

steps.label: Name the four coefficients
steps.margin_note: First mark. Four consecutive coefficients of (1 + x)ⁿ are ⁿCᵣ, ⁿCᵣ₊₁, ⁿCᵣ₊₂, ⁿCᵣ₊₃ for some r.
steps.memory_tip: Four consecutive coefficients start at a general r: ⁿCᵣ to ⁿCᵣ₊₃, never at ⁿC₁.
lines: Take the four consecutive coefficients as
a₁ = ⁿCᵣ, a₂ = ⁿCᵣ₊₁, a₃ = ⁿCᵣ₊₂, a₄ = ⁿCᵣ₊₃

recall.must_convey: That a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄ are ⁿCᵣ, ⁿCᵣ₊₁, ⁿCᵣ₊₂, ⁿCᵣ₊₃.

reject: let them be a one to a four

steps.why: Consecutive coefficients differ only in the lower index, so one letter r fixes all four. Everything after this is algebra in n and r.
common_mistakes: Taking a₁ = ⁿC₁ — the four terms need not start at the beginning.
Using four unrelated letters and having nothing to simplify.

steps.label: Reduce the left side
steps.margin_note: Second to fourth marks. Two identities: ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₊₁ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁, and ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁ = ((n + 1)/(r + 1))·ⁿCᵣ. Together they turn ⁿCᵣ/(ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₊₁) into (r + 1)/(n + 1).
steps.memory_tip: Two identities: ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₊₁ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁, and ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁ = ((n + 1)/(r + 1))·ⁿCᵣ. Together they give (r + 1)/(n + 1).

recall.must_convey: That each fraction on the left becomes ⁿCᵣ over ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁ by Pascal's identity, then (r + 1)/(n + 1) by the ratio identity, so the left side is 2(r + 2)/(n + 1).
accept: use n C r plus n C r plus one equals n plus one C r plus one, then n plus one C r plus one is n plus one by r plus one times n C r, so the first fraction is r plus one by n plus one and the second is r plus three by n plus one
the left side becomes r plus one over n plus one plus r plus three over n plus one which is two r plus four over n plus one
pascal identity in the denominator then the ratio identity gives two into r plus two by n plus one
denominator lo pascal rule vadi, tarvata ratio formula tho r plus one by n plus one vasthundi
left side reduces to two r plus four over n plus one
heard_as: n plus one C r plus one
r plus one by n plus one

steps.why: The sum of two consecutive coefficients is itself a coefficient one row down, and a coefficient one row down is a simple multiple of the one above. Those two facts are the whole proof.
common_mistakes: Writing ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₊₁ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ instead of ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁.
Adding the two fractions before reducing them.

steps.label: Reduce the right side
steps.margin_note: Fifth and sixth marks. The same two identities, one index higher: a₂ + a₃ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₂ = ((n + 1)/(r + 2))·ⁿCᵣ₊₁.
steps.memory_tip: Same two identities one index higher, and keep the factor 2 in front.

recall.must_convey: That the right side is 2ⁿCᵣ₊₁ over ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₂, which by the ratio identity is 2(r + 2)/(n + 1).
accept: the right side is two n C r plus one over n plus one C r plus two which is two into r plus two by n plus one
same identities on the right give two r plus two over n plus one
a two plus a three is n plus one C r plus two and the ratio gives r plus two by n plus one, doubled

r plus two by n plus one

steps.why: The right side is built from the middle pair a₂, a₃, so its reduced form has r + 2 where the left side had r + 1 and r + 3 — which average to r + 2.

steps.label: Match the two sides
steps.margin_note: Seventh mark. (1) and (2) are the same expression — say so in one line.
steps.memory_tip: (1) and (2) are the same expression — write that line, or the last mark is lost.

recall.must_convey: That both sides equal 2(r + 2)/(n + 1), so the identity is proved.
accept: both sides are two r plus two by n plus one so they are equal

steps.why: A show-that question is finished only when the two reduced forms are placed side by side and declared equal.
common_mistakes: Reducing both sides and never writing the concluding line.
